heroHeadline: Ceasefire Holds at Day 499 as Naval Collision Dispute Simmers, Airspace Ban Extended to Oct 24, and PoK Internet Blackout Passes 100 Days
heroSubtitle: September 21, 2026: India's Ministry of External Affairs on September 18 formally rejected Pakistan's account of the September 15 Arabian Sea collision between the Indian Navy destroyer INS Kolkata and the Pakistani corvette PNS Hunain, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal dismissing Islamabad's allegations as 'the usual prevarication'; Pakistan has not issued a further rebuttal, and fault for the incident — the first direct India-Pakistan military encounter since the May 2025 four-day conflict — remains disputed between the two governments. Separately, the Pakistan Airports Authority extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft, in effect since September 17, to October 24, mirroring India's own reciprocal restriction on Pakistani carriers. Across the Line of Control, no firing or infiltration incidents have been recorded since the August 27-29 drone cluster, and the ceasefire holds at Day 499 with no confirmed cross-border fire exchange since May 10, 2025. In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, the internet and mobile-data blackout imposed June 5 amid the JKJAAC-led unrest has now run past 100 days, per NetBlocks, continuing to disrupt banking, commerce and the academic calendar even after the staggered PoK elections concluded in August; independently verified casualty figures for the underlying unrest remain unchanged since JKHRO's early-August count of 89. Bilateral freeze remains otherwise comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT in abeyance despite the August 31 Hague arbitration ruling against India's suspension of the treaty.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
